<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|42|THE GOSPEL|CHA. XV.}}</noinclude>defile a man. but to eate vvith vnvvashen hands, doeth not defile a man.⊣

{{verse|chapter=15|verse=21}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō Thursday the fifth weeke in Lent.}}And IESVS vvent forth from thence and retired into the quarters of Tyre and Sidon. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=22}}† And behold {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 7, 25.''}}* a vvoman of Chanaan came forth out of those coastes, and crying out, sayd to him, Haue mercie vpon me, O lord the Sonne of Dauid: my daughter is sore vexed of a Deuil. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=23}}† VVho ansvvered her not a word. And his Disciples came and besought him saying, Dimisse her: because she crieth out after vs: {{verse|chapter=15|verse=24}}† And he ansvvering said: I was not sent but to the sheepe that are lost of the house of Israel. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=25}}† But she came and adored him, saying, Lord, help me. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=26}}† Who ansvvering, said: It is not good to take the bread of the Children, and to cast it to the dogges. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=27}}† But she said, Yea lord: for the vvhelpes also eate of the crummes that fal from the table of their maisters. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=28}}† Then IESVS ansvvering said to her, O vvoman, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ It were a straunge case that Christ should commend in this woman a sole faith without good workes, that is to say, a dead faith such as could not worke by loue, and which S. Iames doubted not to call the faith not of Christians but of Diuels. ''Aug. de Fid. & Op. c. 16''.}}∷ great is thy faith: be it done to thee as thou vvilt: and her daughter was made hole from that houre.⊣

{{verse|chapter=15|verse=29}}† And when IESVS vvas passed from thence, he came beside the sea of Galilee: and ascending into the mountaine, sate there. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=30}}† And there came to him great multitudes, hauing with them dumme persons, blinde, lame, feeble, and many others: and they cast them dovvne at his feete, and he cured them: {{verse|chapter=15|verse=31}}† so that the multitudes marueled seeing the dumme speake, the lame vvalke, the blinde see: and they magnified the God of Israel. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=32}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 8, 1.''}}* IESVS called together his Disciples, and said: I pitie the multitude: because three dayes novv they continue vvith me, and haue not vvhat to eate: and dimisse them fasting I vvil not, lest they fainte in the vvay. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=33}}† And the disciples say vnto him: vvhence then may vve gette so many loaues in the desert as to fil so great a multitude? {{verse|chapter=15|verse=34}}† And IESVS sayd to them, Hovv many loaues haue you? but they sayd, Seuen, & a fevv litle fishes. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=35}}† And he commaunded the multitude to sit dovvne vpon the ground. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=36}}† And taking the seuen loaues & the fishes, and geuing thankes, he brake, & gaue to his disciples, and {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Here we see againe that the people must not be their owne caruers, nor receiue the Sacraments or other spiritual sustenance immediatly of Christ, or at their owne hand, but of their spiritual gouerners.}}∷ the disciples gaue to the people. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=37}}† And they did al eate, and had their fill. And that vvhich vvas left of the fragments they tooke vp, seuen baskets ful. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=38}}† And there vvere that did eate, foure thousand men, beside children & women. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=39}}† And hauing dimissed the multitude, he vvent vp into a boate, and came into the coastes of Magedan.<noinclude>{{rh|||ANNO-}}</noinclude>
